text:
kevin: Alert — keystore access spike on priv-deploy-nyc-01. Breakglass token used 13x in 6m :fire:
ops-bot: Automated alert from keystore-monitor: high-read-rate; breakglass=true; svc=keystore-agent; region=nyc-01
jess: on it. Can someone paste the affected pod names?
maria: `kubectl -n priv-keystore get pods -o wide | grep keystore-agent` showed keystore-agent-5d7f8 and keystore-agent-5d7f9. Both saw increased GET /v1/keys calls.
samir: grabbing audit logs now. Which KMS backend are we pointing at for that cluster — vault or cloud-hsm?
jess: private deploy uses vault + HSM wrap for that tenant. The breakglass flow goes through vault-unseal service.
kevin: @samir we need the raw audit lines and the vault response headers. Also check RBAC for the breakglass role, it should have MFA enforced.
samir: pulled audit snippet:
```
time=2026-03-21T18:12:03Z method=GET path=/v1/keys/tenant-42 action=wrap response=200 auth.method=token auth.token_id=tb-XXXX role=breakglass
```
samir: token tb-XXXX originates from svcacc-breakglass, last used by user jenkins-batch.
maria: paging RBAC — current role binding for svcacc-breakglass:
```yaml
kind: RoleBinding
subjects:
  - kind: ServiceAccount
    name: svcacc-breakglass
roleRef:
  kind: Role
  name: keystore-breakglass
```
maria: role keystore-breakglass still allows `kv/get` without conditional checks. That looks wrong.
jess: weird — the canary hardening changes from last week were supposed to add a conditional that requires last-auth-method==mfa. Did the migration job run?
erin: migration job failed on priv-deploy-nyc-01 last night, error: `failed to connect to vault-unseal: dial tcp 10.4.2.7:8200: i/o timeout`. Might be related.
kevin: ok — hypothesis: migration didn't complete -> breakglass role not hardened -> automated system used breakglass token (maybe for failover) -> surge of requests. Triage steps: 1) rotate breakglass token 2) revoke token tb-XXXX 3) escalate KMS audit to retention-store 4) patch role to require MFA + source-IP whitelist 5) investigate network flakiness that blocked migration.
jess: I'm rotating tokens now: `vault token-revoke tb-XXXX` then generating new with limited lifetime for manual ops.
samir: also exporting CloudTrail-like audit for host k8s nodes and the vault container logs. Attaching grep of container logs for correlation.
sec-bot: Suspicious pattern: multiple GETs from 3 distinct node IPs within 1m; flagged for potential automated script. Recommend forensic snapshot.
kevin: @maria can you prepare the RBAC patch snippet we want to apply? Keep it minimal — require auth.method=mfa and sourceCIDR to ops floor IPs.
maria: patch:
```yaml
policy: |
  path "kv/*" {
    capabilities = ["read"]
    allowed_params = {
      "auth_method" = ["mfa"]
      "source_ip" = ["10.20.30.0/24"]
    }
  }
```
maria: will open a short-lived canary rollout to one pod, then rollback if anything breaks.
erin: per the runbook, we should also snapshot the host and capture iptables and netpols: `kubectl -n priv-keystore exec -it keystore-agent-5d7f8 -- sh -c \"iptables-save > /tmp/iptables.snap && cat /etc/netpols/*.yaml\"`
jess: running canary apply now with `kubectl apply -f rbac-patch-canary.yaml -n priv-keystore`
kevin: good. post results. If anything unexpected, revert immediately and open incident ticket.
samir: forensic dump uploaded to secure-bucket/forensics/1736000123.tar.gz; included pod logs, host dmesg, and audit lines.
kevin: question: do we have evidence this was malicious or an automated internal job? sec-bot flagged repeated pattern from CI runner user-agent `jenkins/2.401` — that suggests internal automation.
sec-bot: Correlation: jenkins-batch job 4822 started a rolling restart at 18:08 which coincides with vault-unseal connection timeout. Possible race + automated fallback used breakglass.
erin: follow-up: networking team confirmed intermittent BGP flap to the private site at 18:05-18:10 — explains vault connectivity loss.
kevin: summary and next actions: rotate/revoke tokens (done), apply RBAC hardening canary (in progress), increase audit retention for this tenant, add alert to detect breakglass token usage >3x in 5m, and schedule retrospective with CI and networking. Thanks all :thumbsup:
jess: can we add a quick alert rule now? `sec-monitor rule create --name breakglass-spike --expr \"count_over_time(vault_breakglass_requests[5m])>3\" --notify eng-security`
maria: created rule, testing firing on replayed logs.
kevin: great. I'll spin up the postmortem doc and assign owners. Closing thread once canary stabilizes.
